main_text.p: lariam palsi fuerint. Neque tamen horum quenquam legimus vel Zenobia Orientis Reginę[?], licet Christianorum fautrici[?]; vel Tetrico in Galliis rebellanti, adversus hunc Imperatorem, quamuis sanguinarium & in Christianos feraliter debacchantem adhæsisse. Postremò cùm {f}Mnesteus ejus Secretorum Notari-Cuspinia-nus in Au-reliano.us, ad extremum supplicium, ob leue aliquod admissum destinatus, multorū nobilium nomina,cuidam breui (simu-lata manu & sigillo Imperatoris) inser-uisset, quasi etiam ab eodem morti adiudicarentur; ut dū illi se in Imperatorem ulciscerentur, ipse interim sartus tectus effugeret ; quenquam tamen Christianorũ eum vel in facinus attrax-isse, vel adhibuisse in consilium incom-pertum est: cùm tamen eis & infensis-simus esset Imperator, & copia Impera-torem aggrediendi non deesset. Sed in-terim notatu dignum, illum ministrum à Libellis, qui eum occidendum curauit, cognita fraude in stipitem ligatum, bestijs obiectum fuisse.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "trici" in "fautrici" is partly obscured by the page's damage and marked [?]; "Reginę" the final letter is unclear and marked [?]. "lariam" at the top is a fragment of a word from the previous page and is kept as a fragment. The printed "fcraliter" is read as "feraliter". The margin note is read as "Cuspinianus in Aureliano" with hyphenation in the print. The printed spacing before the semicolon ("effugeret ;") and in "nomina,cuidam" is kept as printed. The line "Cap. X." at the foot right is printed in small capitals and is read as a chapter marker; it is given as the signature. The text reads "obiectum" as printed; the ligature forms of long s have been normalised to plain s throughout.
